sents.t: In September, Mr. Lee had a new idea.
“Everybody listens to podcasts these days,” he said.
“What if Oakville Books had its own podcast? We could talk about books and interview local people.”
He asked me to be the host.
“Me? But my accent...” I said.
“Your accent is part of your story,” he answered.
“If I were you, I wouldn’t worry about it.”
We set up two microphones in the back office.
Jake, who studies media at college, agreed to edit the episodes.
Our first guest was Rosa.
She talked about her favorite novel and about her life on Maple Street.
Then I asked her, “If you could meet any writer, alive or dead, who would it be?”
“Maya Angelou,” she said immediately.
“I would thank her for teaching me to be brave.”
For the second episode, I interviewed Walter from the food bank, and for the third, Emma joined us online from Chicago.
At first, only twelve people listened.
But after Rosa’s episode was shared on the town’s community page, we had more than five hundred listeners.
Last week, a woman stopped me in the store.
“Are you Sam from the podcast? I love your show!”
A year ago, I would never have believed it.
